about: India standalone battery storage: tender results (tariffs), EPC order prices and defaults for the cost and break-even tariff calculator. Tariffs are ₹ lakh per MW per month, as discovered in the e-reverse auction. One row per tender; low/high are the lowest and highest winning tariffs. Add new results from the daily news check (see UPDATING.md).

defaults.site_note: India site and contractor costs: transformers, switchyard, civil works, installation, grid connection and the EPC contractor's margin. 2-hour: NTPC's Solapur EPC order (Mar 2026, excluding tax) works out to about US$126/kWh; take away today's landed price of a China 2-hour AC system (about US$87/kWh) and about US$38/kWh is left. 4-hour (assumption): half of these costs scale with power (MW) and half with energy (MWh), giving about US$28.5/kWh.
defaults.om_note: Yearly running cost including battery augmentation, 2.5% of the investment (US NREL Annual Technology Baseline 2024). Indian running costs are probably lower.
defaults.vgf_note: Viability gap funding under the 2025 scheme: ₹18 lakh per MWh, about 70% paid by commercial operation. Set to zero for tenders without VGF.
defaults.tenure_note: Most 2-hour capacity allocated in 2025 was on 12-year contracts (JMK); recent 4-hour tenders (TGGENCO, SECI Odisha, TNGECL) use 15 years.
defaults.finance_note: Assumption: 70% debt at SBI's one-year MCLR (8.70%) and 30% equity expecting 15% a year, the low end of the 15–20% returns lenders expect (JMK). That gives a cost of capital of about 10.6% a year (before tax).
defaults.charging_note: In these tenders the buyer supplies the charging power and pays a fixed monthly charge per MW, so the developer's income is the tariff alone; the break-even tariff covers investment, financing and running costs only.

market_notes.text: India allocated 10.4 GW of standalone storage in 2025; about 75% of the 2-hour capacity was awarded at tariffs JMK and IEEFA class as at risk of not being viable.
Tariffs turned up in 2026: WBSEDCL's 4-hour result was about 25% above a comparable January 2026 tender, and GUVNL's 2-hour result about 10% above February's.
Cells landed in India cost about US$61–66/kWh in August 2026, 14–23% above China after tax.
